Union Finance and Corporate Affairs Minister inaugurates new state-of-the-art building of Income Tax Department 'Aayakar Sindhu' at Nariman Point, Mumbai
articles.full_content:
Smt. Sitharaman urges Income Tax Officers to exercise their authority with empathy, sensitivity and a spirit of public service, ensuring that governance remains citizen-centric
: Mumbai, July 26, 2026
The Union Minister for Finance and Corporate Affairs Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman inaugurated ‘Aayakar Sindhu’, the new state-of-the-art office complex of the Income Tax Department at Nariman Point, Mumbai, and dedicated it to the service of the nation.
Speaking on the occasion which falls on Kargil Vijay Diwas, Union Minister for Finance and Corporate Affairs Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman first paid heartfelt tributes to the brave soldiers who made the supreme sacrifice during the 1999 Kargil War. Emphasising the values of patriotism and public service, she said, "We will ensure every institution of the Republic remains worthy of their sacrifice."
Referring to the newly inaugurated Income Tax Department office, "Aayakar Sindhu", located at Nariman Point, Mumbai, Smt. Sitharaman noted that the locality is named after noted freedom fighter Khurshed Framji Nariman. She urged officers of the Income Tax Department to serve the nation with integrity and dedication as a tribute to the soldiers and freedom fighters who devoted their lives to the country.
Addressing the Income Tax officers, the Finance Minister observed that they are privileged to serve the nation in a highly sensitive role that demands the highest standards of honesty, professionalism and integrity.
Explaining the significance of the name "Aayakar Sindhu", Smt. Sitharaman said it aptly reflects the role of the Income Tax Department. Just as the ocean (Sindhu) receives water from countless rivers, the Department mobilises tax revenues from taxpayers across the country and channels them into the Consolidated Fund of India, from where resources are utilised for nation-building and public welfare.
Smt. Sitharaman spoke about the challenges encountered in clearances and removing encroachments before the construction of Aayakar Sindhu. Stating this, the Finance Minister urged officers to reflect on the difficulties often faced by ordinary citizens in resolving their day-to-day issues. She called upon them to exercise their authority with empathy, sensitivity and a spirit of public service, ensuring that governance remains citizen-centric.
Smt. Sitharaman also assured Income Tax officials that the Government is committed to improving office infrastructure and residential accommodation, particularly in metropolitan cities such as Mumbai, where officials often undertake long commutes due to limited government housing. She informed that efforts are underway to expedite the government-to-government land acquisition process through the Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) for establishing permanent office premises, as several Income Tax offices in Mumbai and Navi Mumbai presently function from rented buildings.

Ministry of Corporate Affairs’ ‘Corporate Mitra Scheme’ Awareness Webinar Successfully Organized by IICA Shillong for the youth and enterprises of Arunachal Pradesh
articles.full_content:
The Indian Institute of Corporate Affairs (IICA), Shillong, under the Ministry of Corporate Affairs, successfully organised a webinar on recently, for awareness and sensitization of the Corporate Mitra Scheme among the youth, students, MSMEs, professionals and enterprises of Arunachal Pradesh.
The webinar was conducted as part of the Corporate Mitra Scheme Awareness Campaign for the Northeast Region (NER), in collaboration with Rajiv Gandhi University (RGU) -Arunachal Pradesh and support of The Institute of Cost Accountants of India (ICMAI) - as the lead co-host and the Institute of Company Secretaries of India (ICSI) , the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI) – as the support co-host.
The Scheme aims to empower MSMEs, primarily in the Tier-3 & 2 cities, by supporting them in playing their part in the larger vision of a Viksit Bharat @ 2047. The scheme embodies the vision of a formalized, financially sustainable, and a thriving MSME sector by creating a strong support ecosystem for the MSMEs, through facilitating access to a pool of qualified, accredited and trusted para professionals “Corporate Mitras”.
The Corporate Mitras are envisaged to provide accessible, affordable, and quality compliance and business support services to Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs), while creating a pool of trained para-professionals by equipping young graduates with industry-relevant knowledge and practical skills. The initiative is expected to strengthen the MSME ecosystem and enhance employment opportunities, particularly across the North Eastern Region. The accredited Corporate Mitra(s) are expected to provide affordable and accessible professional assistance to the local enterprises, for the non-core aspects of their business operation i.e. regulatory, compliance, financial, taxation, accounting, and governance-related needs, thereby ensuring that MSMEs can focus on innovation, expansion and growth, while meeting regulatory requirements with ease.
The scheme implementation is planned with an initial pan India target of 2000 participants, including 200 exclusively from the North East Region (NER), with a 50% fee concession being available for the NER candidates.
For Scheme’s rollout and implementation for the Northeast region, Indian Institute of Corporate Affairs (IICA) Shillong, under the Ministry of Corporate Affairs has been designated as the nodal agency for coordination and liaison with State Governments and other stakeholders (universities/associations/industry bodies/institutes etc.), for promotion, and awareness of the Scheme.
Registration for the 'Corporate Mitra' Course was launched for registration by eligible students w.e.f. from 15th July 2026 and shall be live up till to 31st July 2026 (Registration Link: https://swayamplus.education.gov.in/courses/corporate-mitra).

Centre Allocates ₹2,010 Crore for Judicial Infrastructure and eCourts Modernisation in Union Budget 2026.
articles.full_content:
Under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme (CSS) for Development of Infrastructure Facilities for the District and Subordinate Courts, a sum of Rs. 810 crore has been allocated in the union budget 2026 for judicial infrastructure. In addition, sum of Rs. 1200 crore has been allocated in the union budget 2026 for the eCourts Project Phase-III being implemented for digitisation of courts including necessary training and capacity building programmes. Adequate budgetary provisions are made under these Schemes based on approved outlays and availability of funds. However, the expeditious disposal of cases depends on multiple factors including complexity of case, quality of investigation, availability of relevant evidence and presentation thereof by the Advocates, timely delivery of the court processes, active participation of the parties, judicial procedures etc.

The Government of India, in coordination with the State Government and the Judiciary, has taken several measures to ensure accessible, speedy and effective justice across the country, including in the Tonk–Sawai Madhopur Parliamentary Constituency. Financial assistance is provided under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme (CSS) for strengthening of court infrastructure. Tele-Law services are available through Common Service Centres (CSCs) to provide pre-litigation legal advice. Under the eCourts Project, digital services such as e-Filing, e-Pay, Virtual Courts, video conferencing and the National Judicial Data Grid (NJDG) have been implemented. Free legal aid is extended through the Legal Services Authorities. Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) mechanisms, including Lok Adalats and mediation, are also being promoted for expeditious resolution of disputes.
This information was given by the Union Minister of Law and Justice, Shri Arjun Ram Meghwal Ji, in a written reply to the Lok Sabha.

Review Meeting on Solid Waste Management on Railway Lands Held in Bengaluru
articles.full_content:
A review meeting on solid waste management on Railway lands and within Greater Bengaluru was held today at the Divisional Railway Office, Bengaluru. The meeting was jointly chaired by Hon'ble Union Minister of State for Railways and Jal Shakti, Shri V. Somanna, and Hon'ble Minister for Greater Bengaluru Development, Government of Karnataka, Shri Krishna Byre Gowda.
The meeting discussed the issue of garbage, construction debris and unauthorized dumping of waste on Railway lands. The Ministers reviewed the present situation and emphasized the need for close coordination between the Railways and the Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) to keep Railway lands clean.
During the meeting, Railway officials identified several locations where garbage and debris have accumulated due to unauthorized dumping. Shri V. Somanna directed the officials to remove the waste at the earliest and prepare a comprehensive action plan for clearing Railway lands.
The Hon'ble Minister, Shri V. Somanna, stressed that all concerned agencies, including the Greater Bengaluru Authority, Railways, BWSSB, BESCOM and other civic bodies, should work together under a common coordination mechanism to ensure effective waste management. He also noted that the introduction of bio-toilets in trains has brought a significant improvement in railway sanitation.
He directed that strict action, including the imposition of penalties, be taken against those found dumping garbage or debris on railway land.
Shri Krishna Byre Gowda emphasized the need to make Bengaluru free from waste and said that a month-long cleanliness campaign will be launched from August 1, 2026. He also directed officials to remove weeds growing along Railway tracks and said that preventive measures should be taken to stop future dumping.
Both the Ministers instructed officials to identify and close unauthorized access points that are being used for dumping garbage and construction debris onto Railway property.
Officials of the Greater Bengaluru Authority informed the meeting that scientific methods would be adopted for the disposal of waste and assured full cooperation in implementing long-term solutions.
The meeting was attended by Divisional Railway Manager, Bengaluru Division, Shri Ashutosh Kumar Singh; Chief Commissioner, Greater Bengaluru Authority, Shri Maheshwara Rao; Chairperson, BWSSB, Smt. Manjula; Chief Engineer, K-RIDE, Shri Lakshman Singh; and senior officers from South Western Railway and the Greater Bengaluru Authority.
articles.summary: A review meeting on solid waste management on Railway lands and within Greater Bengaluru was held today at the Divisional Railway Office, Bengaluru. The meeting was jointly chaired by Hon'ble Union Minister of State for Railways and Jal Shakti, Shri V. Somanna, and Hon'ble Minister for Greater Bengaluru Development, Government of Karnataka, Shri Krishna Byre Gowda.
